claim: Official Claude Code docs defining what Skills are, the SKILL.md format, frontmatter fields, dynamic context (!`cmd`), bundled skills, and storage locations.
quote: Skills extend what Claude can do. Create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with /skill-name.

claim: Simon Willison's analysis arguing Skills may be a bigger deal than MCP because they are just Markdown + tiny YAML and load on demand.
quote: Each skill only takes up a few dozen extra tokens, with the full details only loaded in should the user request a task that the skill can help solve. I expect we'll see a Cambrian explosion in Skills which will make this year's MCP rush look pedestrian by comparison.

claim: Side-by-side comparison of CLAUDE.md, slash commands, skills, and subagents — invocation model, context cost, and isolation differences.
quote: Skills: Auto-applied rich workflows / Auto-triggered by description match / Shares main window. Subagents: Research-heavy, multi-step tasks / Auto-delegated or via Task tool / Separate window / Full isolation.

claim: Practical guide on writing skill descriptions: lead with the use condition, avoid vague triggers and capability lists.
quote: Lead with the use condition. 'Use this skill when [X].' The model parses this as a triage rule.

quote: 13.4% of all skills, or 534 in total, all contain at least one critical-level security issue ... 36.82% (1,467 skills) have at least one security flaw. 100% of confirmed malicious skills contain malicious code patterns, while 91% simultaneously employ prompt injection techniques.
